weather: deep winter, short days, frozen ground, dark by 5
insight_headlines: "What is it?" is the question to stop asking.
The seder is possibly the oldest child-centered teaching ritual on earth.
Sorting by material is harder than sorting by color.
Preservation is a surprisingly big idea.

weather: cold and wet, the longest-feeling month, still dark early
insight_headlines: Specific recognition beats general praise, every time.
Outdoor play is the highest-return activity available, and May is when it gets easy.
Children calibrate fear from your face, not from the facts.
Fever makes children clingy, and meeting it shortens it.

weather: mud, wind, first warm afternoons that do not last
insight_headlines: Giving a tour is the best test of understanding there is.
Jumping with both feet is a genuine milestone and it comes later than most parents expect.
Late summer is a low-energy stretch, and lowering the bar is the right response.
Sorting the candy is more interesting to her than eating them.

weather: rain showers, sudden warmth, everything coming up
insight_headlines: Big numbers mean nothing until she's walked them.
Teeth are evidence, and reading evidence is the whole of palaeontology.
Extinct is a hard word, and it's easier than she'd find "dead".
Scorekeeping turns a chaotic game into a calm one.

weather: warm but unreliable, thunderstorms, long light evenings
insight_headlines: The clocks changing costs her more than it costs you.
Illness is a good time to be the one with the ideas rather than the hands.
A job with a visible end is what a recovering child wants.
Dark afternoons change the shape of the day, and the plan has to change with them.

weather: heat arriving, longest days, first properly hot afternoons
insight_headlines: Grinding grain by hand is how she finds out that food used to be work.
Making a material from scratch is rarer than making a thing.
Naming the parts of something ordinary makes it interesting again.
Waiting for cream to turn into butter is a bet she'll want to see through.

weather: heat, thunderstorms, days too hot to be out at noon
insight_headlines: A game with a whistle and rules teaches listening better than being told to listen.
Thinking about what an animal needs in winter is easier than thinking about herself.
Serving other people is a role she'll take more seriously than being served.
A measurement she takes every day teaches more than a fact does.

weather: heavy heat, humid, the flat end of summer
insight_headlines: A rainbow she can make and unmake stops being magic and starts being light.
Naming clouds is the first time the sky has parts.
A scale with pictures lets her rate something she can't measure.
Cold is easier to investigate than hot, because she can hold it.

weather: cooling, first cold mornings, light going earlier
insight_headlines: She thinks water that dries has gone, and it takes seeing it come back to fix that.
Being wrong in a forecast is the most useful kind of wrong.
Sorting the year into four is easier than remembering it.
A tree she's chosen is different from a tree she's shown.

weather: wind and rain, leaves down, dark by 6 after the clocks
insight_headlines: Five months is longer than she can picture, and that's exactly why it's worth doing.
Absence is harder to notice than presence, and it has to be pointed out.
Rotting is the part of nature children are usually protected from, and it's the interesting half.
A collection with a purpose behaves differently from a collection.

weather: grey, wet, dark by 5, the flattest month
insight_headlines: Big gatherings overwhelm her faster than they overwhelm you, and she needs an exit.
A sharp-enough knife is safer than a blunt one, and she can learn a grip.
She can name what she doesn't like once she has words for the tastes.
A constraint is what makes her choose instead of asking for everything.

weather: cold, dark by 4:30, possible snow, indoors a lot
insight_headlines: Doing a job with her feet is how she gets her whole body into it.
Washing up is water play with a result, and she'll do it for the water alone.
Sour is the taste she'll learn to like on purpose, and that's a new experience.
Directing an adult is the strongest evidence of competence she can get.
